7/math.title: Properties and Relationships
7/math.content: use the properties and order of operations, and the relationships between operations, to solve problems involving whole numbers, decimal numbers, fractions, ratios, rates, and percents, including those requiring multiple steps or multiple operations

7/math.title: Math Facts
7/math.content: understand and recall commonly used percents, fractions, and decimal equivalents

7/math.title: Mental Math
7/math.content: use mental math strategies to increase and decrease a whole number by 1%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, and 100%, and explain the strategies used

7/math.title: Addition and Subtraction
7/math.content: use objects, diagrams, and equations to represent, describe, and solve situations involving addition and subtraction of integers

7/math.title: Addition and Subtraction
7/math.content: add and subtract fractions, including by creating equivalent fractions, in various contexts

7/math.title: Multiplication and Division
7/math.content: determine the greatest common factor for a variety of whole numbers up to 144 and the lowest common multiple for two and three whole numbers

7/math.title: Multiplication and Division
7/math.content: evaluate and express repeated multiplication of whole numbers using exponential notation, in various contexts

7/math.title: Multiplication and Division
7/math.content: multiply and divide fractions by fractions, using tools in various contexts

7/math.title: Multiplication and Division
7/math.content: multiply and divide decimal numbers by decimal numbers, in various contexts

7/math.title: Multiplication and Division
7/math.content: identify proportional and non-proportional situations and apply proportional reasoning to solve problems

7/math.title: Patterns and Relationships
7/math.content: identify, describe, extend, create, and make predictions about a variety of patterns, including those found in real-life contexts

7/math.title: Patterns
7/math.content: identify and compare a variety of repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns, including patterns found in real-life contexts, and compare linear growing patterns on the basis of their constant rates and initial values

7/math.title: Patterns
7/math.content: create and translate repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns involving whole numbers and decimal numbers using various representations, including algebraic expressions and equations for linear growing patterns

7/math.title: Patterns
7/math.content: determine pattern rules and use them to extend patterns, make and justify predictions, and identify missing elements in repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns involving whole numbers and decimal numbers, and use algebraic representations of the pattern rules to solve for unknown values in linear growing patterns

7/math.title: Patterns
7/math.content: create and describe patterns to illustrate relationships among integers

7/math.title: Equations and Inequalities
7/math.content: demonstrate an understanding of variables, expressions, equalities, and inequalities, and apply this understanding in various contexts

7/math.title: Variables and Expressions
7/math.content: add and subtract monomials with a degree of 1 that involve whole numbers, using tools

7/math.title: Variables and Expressions
7/math.content: evaluate algebraic expressions that involve whole numbers and decimal numbers

7/math.title: Equalities and Inequalities
7/math.content: solve equations that involve multiple terms, whole numbers, and decimal numbers in various contexts, and verify solutions

7/math.title: Equalities and Inequalities
7/math.content: solve inequalities that involve multiple terms and whole numbers, and verify and graph the solutions

7/math.title: Coding
7/math.content: solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations using coding concepts and skills

7/math.title: Coding Skills
7/math.content: solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing efficient code, including code that involves events influenced by a defined count and/or subprogram and other control structures

7/math.title: Coding Skills
7/math.content: read and alter existing code, including code that involves events influenced by a defined count and/or subprogram and other control structures, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes and the efficiency of the code

7/math.title: Mathematical Modelling
7/math.content: apply the process of mathematical modelling to represent, analyse, make predictions, and provide insight into real-life situations This overall expectation has no specific expectations. Mathematical modelling is an iterative and interconnected process that is applied to various contexts, allowing students to bring in learning from other strands. Students’ demonstration of the process of mathematical modelling, as they apply concepts and skills learned in other strands, is assessed and evaluated. Read more about the mathematical modelling process.

7/math.title: Data Literacy
7/math.content: manage, analyse, and use data to make convincing arguments and informed decisions, in various contexts drawn from real life

7/math.title: Data Collection and Organization
7/math.content: explain why percentages are used to represent the distribution of a variable for a population or sample in large sets of data, and provide examples

7/math.title: Data Collection and Organization
7/math.content: collect qualitative data and discrete and continuous quantitative data to answer questions of interest, and organize the sets of data as appropriate, including using percentages

7/math.title: Data Visualization
7/math.content: select from among a variety of graphs, including circle graphs, the type of graph best suited to represent various sets of data; display the data in the graphs with proper sources, titles, and labels, and appropriate scales; and justify their choice of graphs

7/math.title: Data Visualization
7/math.content: create an infographic about a data set, representing the data in appropriate ways, including in tables and circle graphs, and incorporating any other relevant information that helps to tell a story about the data

7/math.title: Data Analysis
7/math.content: determine the impact of adding or removing data from a data set on a measure of central tendency, and describe how these changes alter the shape and distribution of the data

7/math.title: Data Analysis
7/math.content: analyse different sets of data presented in various ways, including in circle graphs and in misleading graphs, by asking and answering questions about the data, challenging preconceived notions, and drawing conclusions, then make convincing arguments and informed decisions

7/math.title: Probability
7/math.content: describe the likelihood that events will happen, and use that information to make predictions

7/math.title: Probability
7/math.content: describe the difference between independent and dependent events, and explain how their probabilities differ, providing examples

7/math.title: Probability
7/math.content: determine and compare the theoretical and experimental probabilities of two independent events happening and of two dependent events happening

7/math.title: Geometric and Spatial Reasoning
7/math.content: describe and represent shape, location, and movement by applying geometric properties and spatial relationships in order to navigate the world around them

7/math.title: Geometric Reasoning
7/math.content: describe and classify cylinders, pyramids, and prisms according to their geometric properties, including plane and rotational symmetry

7/math.title: Geometric Reasoning
7/math.content: draw top, front, and side views, as well as perspective views, of objects and physical spaces, using appropriate scales

7/math.title: Location and Movement
7/math.content: perform dilations and describe the similarity between the image and the original shape

7/math.title: Location and Movement
7/math.content: describe and perform translations, reflections, and rotations on a Cartesian plane, and predict the results of these transformations

7/math.title: Measurement
7/math.content: compare, estimate, and determine measurements in various contexts

7/math.title: The Metric System
7/math.content: describe the differences and similarities between volume and capacity, and apply the relationship between millilitres (mL) and cubic centimetres (cm3) to solve problems

7/math.title: The Metric System
7/math.content: solve problems involving perimeter, area, and volume that require converting from one metric unit of measurement to another

7/math.title: Circles
7/math.content: use the relationships between the radius, diameter, and circumference of a circle to explain the formula for finding the circumference and to solve related problems

7/math.title: Circles
7/math.content: construct circles when given the radius, diameter, or circumference

7/math.title: Circles
7/math.content: show the relationships between the radius, diameter, and area of a circle, and use these relationships to explain the formula for measuring the area of a circle and to solve related problems

7/math.title: Volume and Surface Area
7/math.content: represent cylinders as nets and determine their surface area by adding the areas of their parts

7/math.title: Volume and Surface Area
7/math.content: show that the volume of a prism or cylinder can be determined by multiplying the area of its base by its height, and apply this relationship to find the area of the base, volume, and height of prisms and cylinders when given two of the three measurements

7/math.title: Money and Finances
7/math.content: demonstrate the knowledge and skills needed to make informed financial decisions

7/math.title: Money Concepts
7/math.content: identify and compare exchange rates, and convert foreign currencies to Canadian dollars and vice versa

7/math.title: Financial Management
7/math.content: identify and describe various reliable sources of information that can help with planning for and reaching a financial goal

7/math.title: Financial Management
7/math.content: create, track, and adjust sample budgets designed to meet longer-term financial goals for various scenarios

7/math.title: Financial Management
7/math.content: identify various societal and personal factors that may influence financial decision making, and describe the effects that each might have

7/math.title: Consumer and Civic Awareness
7/math.content: explain how interest rates can impact savings, investments, and the cost of borrowing to pay for goods and services over time

7/math.title: Consumer and Civic Awareness
7/math.content: compare interest rates and fees for different accounts and loans offered by various financial institutions, and determine the best option for different scenarios

8/math.title: Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) Skills in Mathematics and the Mathematical Processes
Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) Skills and the Mathematical Processes
8/math.content: apply, to the best of their ability, a variety of social-emotional learning skills to support their use of the mathematical processes and their learning in connection with the expectations in the other five strands of the mathematics curriculum

8/math.content: represent and compare very large and very small numbers, including through the use of scientific notation, and describe various ways they are used in everyday life

8/math.title: Rational and Irrational Numbers
8/math.content: describe, compare, and order numbers in the real number system (rational and irrational numbers), separately and in combination, in various contexts

8/math.title: Rational and Irrational Numbers
8/math.content: estimate and calculate square roots, in various contexts

8/math.title: Fractions, Decimals, and Percents
8/math.content: use fractions, decimal numbers, and percents, including percents of more than 100% or less than 1%, interchangeably and flexibly to solve a variety of problems

8/math.title: Math Facts
8/math.content: understand and recall commonly used square numbers and their square roots

8/math.content: add and subtract integers, using appropriate strategies, in various contexts

8/math.title: Addition and Subtraction
8/math.content: add and subtract fractions, using appropriate strategies, in various contexts

8/math.title: Multiplication and Division
8/math.content: multiply and divide fractions by fractions, as well as by whole numbers and mixed numbers, in various contexts

8/math.title: Multiplication and Division
8/math.content: multiply and divide integers, using appropriate strategies, in various contexts

8/math.title: Multiplication and Division
8/math.content: compare proportional situations and determine unknown values in proportional situations, and apply proportional reasoning to solve problems in various contexts

8/math.content: identify, describe, extend, create, and make predictions about a variety of patterns, including those found in real-life contexts

8/math.content: identify and compare a variety of repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns, including patterns found in real-life contexts, and compare linear growing and shrinking patterns on the basis of their constant rates and initial values

8/math.content: create and translate repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns involving rational numbers using various representations, including algebraic expressions and equations for linear growing and shrinking patterns

8/math.content: determine pattern rules and use them to extend patterns, make and justify predictions, and identify missing elements in growing and shrinking patterns involving rational numbers, and use algebraic representations of the pattern rules to solve for unknown values in linear growing and shrinking patterns

8/math.title: Patterns
8/math.content: create and describe patterns to illustrate relationships among rational numbers

8/math.title: Equations and Inequalities
8/math.content: demonstrate an understanding of variables, expressions, equations, and inequalities, and apply this understanding in various contexts

8/math.title: Variables and Expressions
8/math.content: add and subtract monomials with a degree of 1, and add binomials with a degree of 1 that involve integers, using tools

8/math.title: Variables and Expressions
8/math.content: evaluate algebraic expressions that involve rational numbers

8/math.title: Equalities and Inequalities
8/math.content: solve equations that involve multiple terms, integers, and decimal numbers in various contexts, and verify solutions

8/math.title: Equalities and Inequalities
8/math.content: solve inequalities that involve integers, and verify and graph the solutions

8/math.title: Coding
8/math.content: solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations using coding concepts and skills

8/math.title: Coding Skills
8/math.content: solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves the analysis of data in order to inform and communicate decisions

8/math.title: Coding Skills
8/math.content: read and alter existing code involving the analysis of data in order to inform and communicate decisions, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes and the efficiency of the code

8/math.title: Data Literacy
8/math.content: manage, analyse, and use data to make convincing arguments and informed decisions, in various contexts drawn from real life

8/math.title: Data Collection and Organization
8/math.content: identify situations involving one-variable data and situations involving two-variable data, and explain when each type of data is needed

8/math.title: Data Collection and Organization
8/math.content: collect continuous data to answer questions of interest involving two variables, and organize the data sets as appropriate in a table of values

8/math.title: Data Visualization
8/math.content: select from among a variety of graphs, including scatter plots, the type of graph best suited to represent various sets of data; display the data in the graphs with proper sources, titles, and labels, and appropriate scales; and justify their choice of graphs

8/math.title: Data Visualization
8/math.content: create an infographic about a data set, representing the data in appropriate ways, including in tables and scatter plots, and incorporating any other relevant information that helps to tell a story about the data

8/math.title: Data Analysis
8/math.content: use mathematical language, including the terms “strong”, “weak”, “none”, “positive”, and “negative”, to describe the relationship between two variables for various data sets with and without outliers

8/math.title: Data Analysis
8/math.content: analyse different sets of data presented in various ways, including in scatter plots and in misleading graphs, by asking and answering questions about the data, challenging preconceived notions, and drawing conclusions, then make convincing arguments and informed decisions

8/math.title: Probability
8/math.content: describe the likelihood that events will happen, and use that information to make predictions

8/math.title: Probability
8/math.content: solve various problems that involve probability, using appropriate tools and strategies, including Venn and tree diagrams

8/math.title: Probability
8/math.content: determine and compare the theoretical and experimental probabilities of multiple independent events happening and of multiple dependent events happening

8/math.title: Geometric and Spatial Reasoning
8/math.content: describe and represent shape, location, and movement by applying geometric properties and spatial relationships in order to navigate the world around them

8/math.title: Geometric Reasoning
8/math.content: identify geometric properties of tessellating shapes and identify the transformations that occur in the tessellations

8/math.title: Geometric Reasoning
8/math.content: make objects and models using appropriate scales, given their top, front, and side views or their perspective views

8/math.content: use scale drawings to calculate actual lengths and areas, and reproduce scale drawings at different ratios

8/math.title: Location and Movement
8/math.content: describe and perform translations, reflections, rotations, and dilations on a Cartesian plane, and predict the results of these transformations

8/math.title: Measurement
8/math.content: compare, estimate, and determine measurements in various contexts

8/math.title: The Metric System
8/math.content: represent very large (mega, giga, tera) and very small (micro, nano, pico) metric units using models, base ten relationships, and exponential notation

8/math.title: Lines and Angles
8/math.content: solve problems involving angle properties, including the properties of intersecting and parallel lines and of polygons

8/math.title: Length, Area, and Volume
8/math.content: solve problems involving the perimeter, circumference, area, volume, and surface area of composite two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects, using appropriate formulas

8/math.title: Length, Area, and Volume
8/math.content: describe the Pythagorean relationship using various geometric models, and apply the theorem to solve problems involving an unknown side length for a given right triangle

8/math.title: Money and Finances
8/math.content: demonstrate the knowledge and skills needed to make informed financial decisions

8/math.title: Money Concepts
8/math.content: describe some advantages and disadvantages of various methods of payment that can be used when dealing with multiple currencies and exchange rates

8/math.title: Financial Management
8/math.content: create a financial plan to reach a long-term financial goal, accounting for income, expenses, and tax implications

8/math.title: Financial Management
8/math.content: identify different ways to maintain a balanced budget, and use appropriate tools to track all income and spending, for several different scenarios

8/math.title: Financial Management
8/math.content: determine the growth of simple and compound interest at various rates using digital tools, and explain the impact interest has on long-term financial planning

8/math.content: compare various ways for consumers to get more value for their money when spending, including taking advantage of sales and customer loyalty and incentive programs, and determine the best choice for different scenarios

8/math.content: compare interest rates, annual fees, and rewards and other incentives offered by various credit card companies and consumer contracts to determine the best value and the best choice for different scenarios

1/language.title: Transferable Skills
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of how the seven transferable skills (critical thinking and problem solving; innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurship; self-directed learning; collaboration; communication; global citizenship and sustainability; and digital literacy) are used in various language and literacy contexts

1/language.title: Receptive and Expressive Communication
1/language.content: identify how transferable skills can be used to support communication in various cultural, social, linguistic, and domain-specific contexts, and apply them when reading, listening to, viewing, and creating texts of various forms

1/language.title: Student Agency and Engagement
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of how transferable skills help them to express their voice and be engaged in their learning

1/language.title: Digital Media Literacy
1/language.content: demonstrate and apply the knowledge and skills needed to interact safely and responsibly in online environments, use digital and media tools to construct knowledge, and demonstrate learning as critical consumers and creators of media

1/language.title: Digital Citizenship
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of their rights and responsibilities when interacting online with appropriate permission, and make decisions that contribute positively to the development of their digital identity and those of their communities

1/language.title: Online Safety, Well-Being, and Etiquette
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of how to navigate online environments safely, manage their privacy, and interact in a way that supports their well-being and that of others, including seeking appropriate permission

1/language.title: Research and Information Literacy
1/language.content: gather, evaluate, and use information, considering various perspectives, to construct knowledge and demonstrate learning

1/language.title: Forms, Conventions, and Techniques
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of the forms, conventions, and techniques of digital and media texts, and apply this understanding when analyzing texts

1/language.title: Media, Audience, and Production
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of the interrelationships between the form, message, and context of a text, the audience, and the creator

1/language.title: Innovation and Design
1/language.content: use digital and media tools to support stages of the design process and to develop creative solutions to authentic, real-world problems

1/language.title: Community and Cultural Awareness
1/language.content: communicate and collaborate with various communities in a safe, respectful, responsible, and inclusive manner when using online platforms and environments, including digital and media tools, and demonstrate cultural awareness with members of the community

1/language.title: Applications, Connections, and Contributions
1/language.content: apply language and literacy skills in cross-curricular and integrated learning, and demonstrate an understanding of, and make connections to, diverse voices, experiences, perspectives, histories, and contributions, including those of First Nations, Métis, and Inuit individuals, communities, groups, and nations

1/language.title: Cross-Curricular and Integrated Learning
1/language.content: apply the knowledge and skills developed in this grade to support learning in various subject areas and identify some ways this learning can be used in everyday life

1/language.title: Identity and Community
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of the contributions, lived experiences, and perspectives of a diversity of individuals and communities, including those in Canada, by exploring the concepts of identity, self, and sense of belonging in culturally responsive and relevant texts

1/language.title: First Nations, Métis, and Inuit Perspectives and Ways of Knowing
1/language.content: identify themes explored in First Nations, Métis, and Inuit cultures to demonstrate an understanding of the varied identities, perspectives, relationships, legacies, truths, and ways of knowing, being, and doing

1/language.title: Oral and Non-Verbal Communication
1/language.content: apply listening, speaking, and non-verbal communication skills and strategies to understand and communicate meaning in formal and informal contexts and for various purposes and audiences

1/language.title: Effective Listening Skills
1/language.content: use effective listening skills, including listening attentively and asking relevant questions, in formal and informal contexts, including conversations and classroom activities

1/language.title: Listening Strategies for Comprehension
1/language.content: identify and use listening strategies before, during, and after listening to comprehend information communicated orally and non-verbally

1/language.title: Speaking Purposes and Strategies
1/language.content: identify the purpose and audience for speaking in formal and informal contexts, and use appropriate speaking strategies, including taking turns, understanding when to speak, and knowing how much to say, to communicate clearly and coherently

1/language.title: Oral and Non-Verbal Communication Strategies
1/language.content: identify and use oral and non-verbal communication strategies, including expression, gestures, and body language, to interpret or contribute to the meaning of messages

1/language.title: Word Choice, Syntax, and Grammar in Oral Communication
1/language.content: use appropriate word choice, including new vocabulary, grammar, and cohesive phrases and sentences when speaking and communicating ideas

1/language.title: Language Foundations for Reading and Writing
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of foundational language knowledge and skills, and apply this understanding when reading and writing

1/language.title: Phonemic Awareness
1/language.content: use understanding of the sound structure of spoken words to orally isolate, blend, and segment phonemes, from simple structures with two phonemes to structures with more phonemes

1/language.title: Alphabetic Knowledge
1/language.content: name and form the upper- and lowercase letters both in and out of order and demonstrate knowledge of alphabetic order, with automaticity

1/language.title: Phonics: Grapheme-Phoneme Correspondence
1/language.content: identify, read, and spell most common grapheme-phoneme correspondences of consonants and vowels, with automaticity

1/language.title: Word-Level Reading and Spelling: Using Phonics Knowledge
1/language.content: use phonics knowledge and phonemic blending to read words, and phonemic segmentation to spell phonetically regular words, in isolation and various text contexts

1/language.title: Word-Level Reading and Spelling: Using Orthographic Knowledge
1/language.content: use developing orthographic knowledge, including position-based tendencies, to make a spelling choice or accurately pronounce a word when reading

1/language.title: Word-Level Reading and Spelling: Using Morphological Knowledge
1/language.content: use developing knowledge of the meanings of words and common morphemes (i.e., bases, prefixes, and suffixes) to read and spell words

1/language.title: Vocabulary
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of commonly used words, acquire and use explicitly taught vocabulary in various contexts, including other subject areas, and use their developing morphological knowledge to analyze and understand new words in context

1/language.title: Reading Fluency: Accuracy, Rate, and Prosody
1/language.content: read simple words, short sentences, and paragraphs in a variety of texts fluently, with accuracy and appropriate pacing to support comprehension, and read aloud with expression

1/language.title: Language Conventions for Reading and Writing
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of sentence structure, grammar, cohesive ties, and capitalization and punctuation, and apply this knowledge when reading and writing sentences, paragraphs, and a variety of texts

1/language.title: Syntax and Sentence Structure
1/language.content: identify and construct simple and compound sentences, including declarative, imperative, interrogative, and exclamatory sentences

1/language.title: Grammar
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of the functions of parts of speech in sentences, including common singular and plural nouns, using the pronoun “I”, the past, present, and future verb tenses, common adjectives and adverbs, and common conjunctions, and use this knowledge to support comprehension and communicate meaning clearly

1/language.title: Capitalization and Punctuation
1/language.content: use their understanding of the meaning and function of capitalization and punctuation to communicate meaning clearly, including the use of a capital letter at the beginning of a sentence and the appropriate punctuation mark at the end

1/language.title: Comprehension: Understanding and Responding to Texts
Knowledge about Texts
1/language.content: apply foundational knowledge and skills to understand a variety of texts, including digital and media texts, by creators with diverse identities, perspectives, and experience, and demonstrate an understanding of the patterns, features, and elements of style associated with various text forms and genres

1/language.title: Using Foundational Knowledge and Skills to Comprehend Texts
1/language.content: read and comprehend short, simple texts, using knowledge of words, grammar, cohesive ties, sentence structures, and background knowledge

1/language.title: Text Forms and Genres
1/language.content: identify simple literary and informational text forms and their associated genres

1/language.title: Text Patterns and Features
1/language.content: identify some text patterns, such as sequencing and chronological order, and text features, including illustrations, symbols, and titles, associated with various text forms, and explain how they help readers, listeners, and viewers understand the meaning

1/language.title: Visual Elements of Texts
1/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between simple illustrations, images, and graphics and the text

1/language.title: Elements of Style
1/language.content: identify some simple elements of style in texts, including voice, word choice, word patterns, and sentence structure, and describe how they help communicate meaning

1/language.title: Point of View
1/language.content: identify the narrator’s point of view in a variety of texts, and suggest an alternative point of view to tell the story

1/language.title: Indigenous Context of Various Text Forms
1/language.content: read, listen to, and view various forms of texts by diverse First Nations, Métis, and Inuit creators to demonstrate understanding of various aspects of First Nations, Métis, and Inuit histories, cultures, relationships, communities, groups, nations, and lived experiences

1/language.title: Comprehension Strategies
1/language.content: apply comprehension strategies before, during, and after reading, listening to, and viewing a variety of texts, including digital and media texts, by creators with diverse identities, perspectives, and experience, in order to understand and clarify the meaning of texts

1/language.title: Prereading: Activating Prior Knowledge
1/language.content: activate prior knowledge, including knowledge gained from personal and text experiences, that they can use to understand the topics of new texts

1/language.title: Prereading: Identifying the Purpose for Reading, Listening, and Viewing
1/language.content: identify purposes for engaging with texts, including enjoyment or finding information

1/language.title: Monitoring of Understanding: Making and Confirming Predictions
1/language.content: make predictions using background knowledge, text features, and evidence from the text

1/language.title: Monitoring of Understanding: Ongoing Comprehension Check
1/language.content: use strategies such as rereading, visualizing, and asking questions, to monitor their understanding of simple texts

1/language.title: Monitoring of Understanding: Making Connections
1/language.content: identify connections between ideas expressed in simple texts and their knowledges and lived experiences, the ideas in other familiar texts, and the world around them

1/language.title: Summarizing: Identifying Relevant Information and Drawing Conclusions
1/language.content: identify important information in a simple text, including the main idea

1/language.title: Reflecting on Learning
1/language.content: identify strategies, such as activating prior knowledge and visualizing, that have helped them comprehend texts

1/language.title: Critical Thinking in Literacy
1/language.content: apply critical thinking skills to deepen understanding of texts, and analyze how various perspectives and topics are communicated and addressed in a variety of texts, including digital, media, and cultural texts

1/language.title: Literary Devices
1/language.content: identify simple literary devices, including rhyme, alliteration, and onomatopoeia, and describe how they help communicate meaning

1/language.title: Making Inferences
1/language.content: make simple inferences, using stated and implied information and ideas, to understand simple texts

1/language.title: Analyzing Texts
1/language.content: analyze simple texts, including literary and informational texts, by identifying and sequencing important information and events

1/language.title: Analyzing Cultural Elements of Texts
1/language.content: identify some cultural elements represented in various texts, including symbols and values, and explain how these elements contribute to the meaning

1/language.title: Perspectives within Texts
1/language.content: identify explicit and implicit perspectives communicated in a text, and describe how these perspectives could influence an audience

1/language.title: Analysis and Response
1/language.content: express personal thoughts and feelings about ideas presented in texts, such as ideas about diversity, inclusion, and accessibility

1/language.title: Indigenous Contexts
1/language.content: identify some ways in which texts created by First Nations, Métis, and Inuit individuals, communities, groups, or nations communicate about historical periods, cultural experiences, and events, and how they relate to current lived experiences

1/language.title: Reflecting on Learning
1/language.content: identify thinking skills that helped them understand simple texts

1/language.title: Composition: Expressing Ideas and Creating Texts
Developing Ideas and Organizing Content

1/language.title: Purpose and Audience
1/language.content: identify the topic, purpose, and audience for various simple texts they plan to create

1/language.title: Developing Ideas
1/language.content: generate ideas about given and chosen topics, using simple strategies and drawing on various resources, including their own lived experiences, and learning from other subject areas

1/language.title: Creating Texts

1/language.content: draft short, simple texts of various forms and genres, including personal narratives, persuasive texts, and procedural texts, using a variety of media, tools, and strategies

1/language.content: print letters and words with appropriate formation patterns, size, placement, and spacing

1/language.title: Producing Final Texts
1/language.content: produce final texts, using simple techniques, to achieve the intended effect

7/language.content: edit draft texts to improve accuracy and style, checking for errors in spelling, punctuation, grammar, and format; edit digital texts using word-processing software, including spell- and grammar-checkers

7/language.title: Publishing, Presenting, and Reflecting
7/language.content: select suitable and effective media, techniques, and tools to publish and present final texts, and critically analyze how well the texts address various topics

7/language.title: Producing Final Texts
7/language.content: produce final texts, selecting a variety of suitable techniques and tools, including digital design and production tools, to achieve the intended effect

7/language.title: Publishing and Presenting Texts
7/language.content: publish and present texts they have created, using various media and tools, and analyze how their choices helped them communicate their intended message

7/language.title: Reflecting on Learning
7/language.content: compare how various strategies and tools helped them communicate their intended message when publishing and presenting texts, analyze how their texts address various topics, and suggest steps for future improvement as a text creator

8/language.title: Transferable Skills
8/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of how the seven transferable skills (critical thinking and problem solving; innovation, creativity, and entrepreneurship; self-directed learning; collaboration; communication; global citizenship and sustainability; and digital literacy) are used in various language and literacy contexts

8/language.title: Receptive and Expressive Communication
8/language.content: analyze and explain how transferable skills can be used to support communication in various cultural, social, linguistic, and domain-specific contexts, and apply them when reading, listening to, viewing, and creating texts of various forms

8/language.title: Student Agency and Engagement
8/language.content: evaluate and explain how transferable skills help them to express their voice, be engaged in their learning, and implement a plan to develop their capabilities and potential

8/language.title: Digital Media Literacy
8/language.content: demonstrate and apply the knowledge and skills needed to interact safely and responsibly in online environments, use digital and media tools to construct knowledge, and demonstrate learning as critical consumers and creators of media

8/language.title: Digital Citizenship
8/language.content: evaluate and explain their rights and responsibilities when interacting online with appropriate permission, and make decisions that contribute positively to the development of their digital identity and those of their communities

8/language.title: Online Safety, Well-Being, and Etiquette
8/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of how to navigate online environments safely, manage their privacy, personal data, and security, and interact in a way that supports their well-being and that of others, including seeking appropriate permission

8/language.title: Research and Information Literacy
8/language.content: conduct research, considering accuracy, credibility, and perspectives, with a focus on misinformation, disinformation, and curated information, to construct knowledge, create texts, and demonstrate learning, while respecting legal and ethical considerations

8/language.title: Forms, Conventions, and Techniques
8/language.content: evaluate the use of the various forms, conventions, and techniques of digital and media texts, consider the impact on the audience, and apply this understanding when analyzing and creating texts

8/language.title: Media, Audience, and Production
8/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of the interrelationships between the form, message, and context of texts, the intended and unintended audience, and the purpose for production

8/language.title: Innovation and Design
8/language.content: select and use appropriate digital and media tools to support the design process and address authentic, relevant, real-world problems by developing and proposing innovative solutions

8/language.title: Community and Cultural Awareness
8/language.content: communicate and collaborate with various communities in a safe, respectful, responsible, and inclusive manner when using online platforms and environments, including digital and media tools, and demonstrate and model cultural awareness with members of the community

8/language.title: Applications, Connections, and Contributions
8/language.content: apply language and literacy skills in cross-curricular and integrated learning, and demonstrate an understanding of, and make connections to, diverse voices, experiences, perspectives, histories, and contributions, including those of First Nations, Métis, and Inuit individuals, communities, groups, and nations

8/language.title: Cross-Curricular and Integrated Learning
8/language.content: analyze and explain how the knowledge and skills developed in this grade support learning in various subject areas and in everyday life, and describe how they enhance understanding and communication

8/language.title: Identity and Community
8/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of the historical contexts, contributions, lived experiences, and perspectives of a diversity of individuals and communities, including those in Canada, by exploring and analyzing the concepts of identity, self, and sense of belonging in a variety of culturally responsive and relevant texts

8/language.title: First Nations, Métis, and Inuit Perspectives and Ways of Knowing
8/language.content: analyze themes explored in First Nations, Métis, and Inuit cultures to demonstrate an understanding of the varied identities, perspectives, relationships, legacies, truths, and ways of knowing, being, and doing

8/language.title: Oral and Non-Verbal Communication
8/language.content: apply listening, speaking, and non-verbal communication skills and strategies to understand and communicate meaning in formal and informal contexts and for various purposes and audiences

8/language.title: Effective Listening Skills
8/language.content: evaluate and use various effective listening skills to enhance comprehension, including paraphrasing, asking open-ended questions, making relevant responses in group discussions, and reflecting on what has been said, and use these skills in formal and informal contexts and for various purposes

8/language.title: Listening Strategies for Comprehension
8/language.content: select and use a variety of listening strategies before, during, and after listening to analyze and comprehend information communicated orally and non-verbally, seek clarification, and identify relevant evidence to support a response appropriate to the context

8/language.title: Speaking Purposes and Strategies
8/language.content: analyze the purpose and audience for speaking in formal and informal contexts, and select and adapt speaking strategies to communicate clearly and coherently

8/language.title: Oral and Non-Verbal Communication Strategies
8/language.content: identify and use oral and non-verbal communication strategies, including expression, gestures, and body language, and evaluate and compare the effectiveness of these strategies in supporting understanding or communication, including how their use may vary across cultures

8/language.title: Word Choice, Syntax, and Grammar in Oral Communication
8/language.content: use precise and descriptive word choice, including domain-specific vocabulary from various subjects, and cohesive and coherent sentences during formal and informal communication, to support audience comprehension

8/language.title: Language Foundations for Reading and Writing
8/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of foundational language knowledge and skills, and apply this understanding when reading and writing

8/language.title: Word-Level Reading and Spelling: Using Morphological Knowledge
8/language.content: use consolidated knowledge of the meanings of words and morphemes (i.e., bases, prefixes, and suffixes) to read and spell complex words with accuracy and automaticity

8/language.title: Vocabulary
8/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of a wide variety of words, acquire and use explicitly taught vocabulary flexibly in various contexts, including other subject areas, and use consolidated morphological knowledge to analyze and understand new words in context

8/language.title: Reading Fluency: Accuracy, Rate, and Prosody
8/language.content: read a variety of complex texts fluently, with accuracy and appropriate pacing, to support comprehension, and when reading aloud, adjust expression and intonation according to the purpose of reading

8/language.title: Language Conventions for Reading and Writing
8/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of sentence structure, grammar, cohesive ties, and capitalization and punctuation, and apply this knowledge when reading and writing sentences, paragraphs, and a variety of texts

8/language.title: Syntax and Sentence Structure
8/language.content: use their knowledge of sentence types and forms to construct increasingly complex sentences that connect and communicate ideas accurately and effectively

8/language.title: Grammar
8/language.content: demonstrate an understanding of the functions of parts of speech in sentences, refine their understanding of grammar, and use this knowledge to support comprehension and communicate meaning clearly and precisely

8/language.title: Capitalization and Punctuation
8/language.content: use and refine their understanding of the meaning and function of capitalization and punctuation to communicate meaning clearly and coherently, when reading and writing

8/language.title: Comprehension: Understanding and Responding to Texts
Knowledge about Texts
8/language.content: apply foundational knowledge and skills to understand a variety of texts, including digital and media texts, by creators with diverse identities, perspectives, and experience, and demonstrate an understanding of the patterns, features, and elements of style associated with various texts forms and genres

8/language.title: Using Foundational Knowledge and Skills to Comprehend Texts
8/language.content: read and comprehend various complex texts, using knowledge of words, grammar, cohesive ties, sentence structures, and background knowledge

8/language.title: Text Forms and Genres
8/language.content: analyze and compare the characteristics of various text forms and genres, including cultural text forms, and provide evidence to explain how they help communicate meaning

8/language.title: Text Patterns and Features
8/language.content: compare the text patterns, such as problem-solution in a letter to the editor, and text features, such as a glossary and infographics, associated with different text forms, including cultural texts, and evaluate their importance in helping readers, listeners, and viewers understand the meaning

8/language.title: Visual Elements of Texts
8/language.content: evaluate how images, graphics, and visual design create, communicate, and contribute to meaning in a variety of texts

8/language.title: Elements of Style
8/language.content: identify various elements of style in texts, including voice, word choice, word patterns, and sentence structure, and analyze how each element helps create meaning and is appropriate for the text form and genre

8/language.title: Point of View
8/language.content: analyze the narrator’s point of view, including limited, omniscient, or unreliable, in a variety of texts, explain how it is communicated, and suggest alternative points of view, giving reasons

8/language.title: Indigenous Context of Various Text Forms
8/language.content: read, listen to, and view a wide variety of text forms by diverse First Nations, Métis, and Inuit creators to make meaning through Indigenous Storywork about First Nations, Métis, and Inuit histories, cultures, relationships, communities, groups, nations, and lived experiences

8/language.title: Comprehension Strategies
8/language.content: apply comprehension strategies before, during, and after reading, listening to, and viewing a variety of texts, including digital and media texts, by creators with diverse identities, perspectives, and experience, in order to understand and clarify the meaning of texts

8/language.title: Prereading: Activating Prior Knowledge
8/language.content: identify and explain prior knowledge from various sources, including personal experiences and learning in other subject areas, that they can use to make connections and understand new texts

8/language.title: Prereading: Identifying the Purpose for Reading, Listening, and Viewing
8/language.content: identify a variety of purposes for engaging with texts, select texts from diverse creators that are suitable for the purposes, and explain why the selections are appropriate

8/language.title: Monitoring of Understanding: Making and Confirming Predictions
8/language.content: make predictions using background knowledge and textual information, pose questions to confirm or refute their predictions, and revise or refine their understanding as indicated

8/language.title: Monitoring of Understanding: Ongoing Comprehension Check
8/language.content: select suitable strategies, such as rereading, using the glossary, asking questions, and consulting references and other resources, to monitor and confirm their understanding of complex texts and solve comprehension problems

8/language.title: Monitoring of Understanding: Making Connections
8/language.content: connect, compare, and contrast the ideas expressed in texts and their knowledges and lived experiences, the ideas in other texts, and the world around them

8/language.title: Summarizing: Identifying Relevant Information and Drawing Conclusions
8/language.content: summarize and synthesize the important ideas and supporting details in complex texts, and draw effective conclusions

8/language.title: Reflecting on Learning
8/language.content: explain and compare how various strategies, such as visualizing, making predictions, summarizing, and connecting to their experiences, have helped them comprehend various texts, and set goals for future improvement

8/language.title: Critical Thinking in Literacy
8/language.content: apply critical thinking skills to deepen understanding of texts, and analyze how various perspectives and topics are communicated and addressed in a variety of texts, including digital, media, and cultural texts

8/language.title: Literary Devices
8/language.content: analyze literary devices, including irony, satire, and allusion, in a variety of texts, and explain how they help create meaning and are appropriate for the intended purpose and audience

8/language.title: Making Inferences
8/language.content: make local and global inferences, using explicit and implicit evidence, to explain and support their interpretations about various complex texts

8/language.title: Analyzing Texts
8/language.content: analyze complex texts, including literary and informational texts, by evaluating, synthesizing, and sequencing relevant information and formulating conclusions

8/language.title: Analyzing Cultural Elements of Texts
8/language.content: analyze cultural elements that are represented in various texts, including norms, values, social hierarchy, pastimes, language, and taboos, by investigating the meanings of these elements, making connections to their lived experience and culture, and considering how the inclusion of these elements contributes to the meaning of the text

8/language.title: Perspectives within Texts
8/language.content: analyze explicit and implicit perspectives communicated in various texts, evaluate any evidence that could suggest bias in these perspectives, and suggest ways to avoid any such bias

8/language.title: Analysis and Response
8/language.content: analyze how various topics, such as diversity, inclusion, and accessibility, are addressed in texts, respond to the insights and messages conveyed, and identify different positions presented

8/language.title: Indigenous Contexts
8/language.content: compare the ways in which historical periods, cultural experiences, and/or socio-political conditions and events have influenced two or more texts created by First Nations, Métis, and Inuit individuals, communities, groups, or nations, and how they relate to current lived experiences

8/language.title: Reflecting on Learning
8/language.content: assess the effectiveness of the critical thinking skills they used when analyzing and evaluating various texts, and set goals to improve their use

8/language.title: Composition: Expressing Ideas and Creating Texts
Developing Ideas and Organizing Content
8/language.content: plan, develop ideas, gather information, and organize content for creating texts of various forms, including digital and media texts, on a variety of topics

8/language.title: Purpose and Audience
8/language.content: identify the topic, purpose, and audience for various texts they plan to create; choose a text form, genre, and medium to suit the purpose and audience, and justify their choices

8/language.title: Developing Ideas
8/language.content: generate and develop ideas and details about challenging topics, such as topics related to diversity, equity, and inclusion and to other subject areas, using a variety of strategies, and drawing on various resources, including their own lived experiences

8/language.title: Research
8/language.content: gather and synthesize information and content relevant to a topic, using a variety of textual sources and appropriate strategies; evaluate the currency, quality, bias, and accuracy of information; verify the reliability of sources; and cite the sources of all content created by others

8/language.title: Organizing Content
8/language.content: classify and sequence ideas and collected information, selecting effective strategies and tools, and identify and organize relevant content, evaluating the choices of text form, genre, and medium, and considering alternatives

8/language.title: Reflecting on Learning
8/language.content: evaluate the strategies and tools used to develop ideas and organize content for texts of the chosen forms, genres, and media, explain which were most helpful, and suggest steps for future improvement as a text creator

8/language.title: Creating Texts
8/language.content: apply knowledge and understanding of various text forms and genres to create, revise, edit, and proofread their own texts, using a variety of media, tools, and strategies, and reflect critically on created texts

8/language.title: Producing Drafts
8/language.content: draft complex texts of various forms and genres, including narrative, persuasive, expository, and informational texts, citing sources, and use a variety of appropriate media, tools, and strategies to transform information and communicate ideas

8/language.title: Printing, Handwriting, and Word Processing
8/language.content: write in cursive fluently, with a personal style, and apply advanced word-processing skills to improve the accuracy and effect of texts

8/language.title: Voice
8/language.content: establish an identifiable voice in their texts, modifying language and style to suit the text’s form, genre, audience, and purpose, and express their thoughts, feelings, and opinions about the topic clearly

8/language.title: Point of View and Perspective
8/language.content: explain the explicit and implicit points of view, perspectives, and bias conveyed in their texts, evaluate how various audiences might respond, and suggest ways to acknowledge other perspectives

8/language.title: Revision
8/language.content: make revisions to the content, elements of style, patterns, and features of draft texts, and add, delete, revise, and reorganize sentences to improve clarity, focus, and coherence, using various strategies and seeking and selectively using feedback

8/language.title: Editing and Proofreading
8/language.content: edit draft texts to improve accuracy and style, checking for errors in spelling, punctuation, grammar, and format; edit digital texts using word-processing software, including spell- and grammar-checkers

8/language.title: Publishing, Presenting, and Reflecting
8/language.content: select suitable and effective media, techniques, and tools to publish and present final texts, and critically analyze how well the texts address various topics

8/language.title: Producing Final Texts
8/language.content: produce final texts using appropriate techniques and tools, including digital design and production tools, to achieve the intended effect

8/language.title: Publishing and Presenting Texts
8/language.content: publish and present texts they have created, using various media and tools, and evaluate how their choices helped them communicate their intended message

8/language.title: Reflecting on Learning
8/language.content: evaluate the strategies and tools they found helpful when publishing and presenting texts, reflect on what they learned at each stage of the creative process, analyze how their texts address various topics, and suggest steps for future improvement as a text creator

k/all.title: Oral and Non-Verbal Communication
k/all.content: communicate orally and non-verbally
listen and respond
use language conventions and non-verbal communication
understand and use new words and develop morphological awareness

k/all.title: Foundations for Reading and Writing
k/all.content: apply early reading and writing skills
name upper- and lowercase letters (both in and out of order)
use proper formation patterns to write letters
isolate and blend phonemes, and segment simple words into phonemes
identify simple grapheme-phoneme correspondences
read and spell simple words using phonemic awareness and phonics knowledge
read short sentences fluently, including those with explicitly taught words, with increasing accuracy, to support comprehension

k/all.title: Understanding and Responding to Texts
k/all.content: understand and respond to a variety of texts by diverse creators from Canada and by diverse First Nations, Métis, and Inuit creators
identify purposes for choosing different texts
apply knowledge of words, sentence structure, and punctuation
read and understand simple texts, using background knowledge and beginning knowledge of words, grammar, and sentence structure
express personal thoughts and feelings about texts
make predictions about unfamiliar texts, using background knowledge
make connections to a variety of texts

k/all.title: Expressing Ideas and Creating Texts
k/all.content: create texts using foundational language knowledge and skills
use knowledge of letters, words, and sentences, with pictures and symbols, to create simple texts
use classroom writing resources to support creating simple texts

k/all.title: The Mathematical Processes
k/all.content: apply the mathematical processes (i.e., problem solving; reasoning and proving; reflecting; connecting; communicating; representing; and selecting tools and strategies)

k/all.title: Number Sense and Operations
k/all.content: use numbers and operations
explore what numbers are used for
understand when counting forward, the quantity gets bigger and when counting backward, the quantity gets smaller
identify and write numbers to 20
subitize quantities to 5
compose and decompose quantities to 10
understand the concept of more than, the same (equal), or less than
estimate the number of objects in small collections and check by counting
count to 20 by 1s, starting from any number
solve equal-share problems using concrete materials
describe relationships between any two numbers from 0 to 20
recall addition facts to 5 and related subtraction facts
solve situations involving addition and subtraction to 10 using concrete materials
identify and explore the value of Canadian coins to 25¢ and coins and bills to $10

k/all.title: Patterns and Relationships
k/all.content: investigate repeating patterns
identify, describe, and create patterns
identify the core of a repeating pattern and describe why it is important
show that patterns can be represented in different ways because the core remains the same
extend patterns in both directions and identify any missing elements

k/all.title: Data Literacy and Probability
k/all.content: collect and display data to answer questions and communicate information, and explore probability in everyday contexts
sort objects or data using one attribute
collect and record data to answer questions of interest, and display it in concrete graphs or picture graphs
respond to data in concrete graphs and picture graphs by interpreting it and drawing conclusions
describe how likely familiar events are to happen

k/all.title: Geometric and Spatial Reasoning
k/all.content: describe two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects, and the location and movement of people and objects
identify, sort, and compare the most common two-dimensional shapes, including circle, hexagon, rhombus, and trapezoid
identify, sort, and compare the most common three-dimensional objects, including cube, sphere, prisms, cone, and pyramid
in structures they have made, identify three-dimensional objects and two-dimensional shapes
construct two-dimensional pictures and three-dimensional structures with matching halves
put two-dimensional shapes together to make other shapes, break them into smaller shapes, and put them together in different ways
describe basic spatial relationships and movements, and visualize objects from different perspectives
give and follow directions for moving from one location to another

k/all.title: Measurement
k/all.content: describe and compare the length, area, mass, or capacity of a variety of objects
describe different ways that objects can be measured
compare the length, area, mass, and capacity of objects using concrete materials

k/all.title: Coding Skills
k/all.content: use foundational coding concepts and skills
use directional and positional language to create and follow instructions involving movement
test and refine instructions
communicate and record step-by-step instructions using symbols, words, or pictures

k/all.title: Scientific Investigation and Engineering Design
k/all.content: use an inquiry process to engage in scientific investigations and to design, build, and test models and structures
state problems and pose questions
make predictions and observations while exploring, investigating, and designing
select materials and tools to carry out investigations and to construct models and structures
draw conclusions and communicate results
design, build, and test models and structures
follow safety rules to help prevent injuries, including concussion, and demonstrate an understanding of the importance of these practices

k/all.title: Exploring Environments
k/all.content: investigate natural and built environments
ask questions about and describe some natural occurrences
sort and classify groups of living and non-living things
compare patterns in natural and built environments

k/all.title: Social Skills
k/all.content: identify and use social skills in play and other contexts
act and talk with peers and adults by expressing and accepting positive messages
show the ability to take turns
demonstrate an awareness of ways of making and keeping friends
use problem-solving skills in social situations

k/all.title: Self-Regulation
k/all.content: demonstrate independence, self-regulation, and a willingness to take on responsibility
demonstrate self-reliance and a sense of responsibility
demonstrate a willingness to try new experiences and to adapt to new situations
demonstrate self-motivation, initiative, and confidence in their approach to learning
demonstrate self-control and adapt behaviour to different contexts
develop empathy for others, and acknowledge and respond to each other’s feelings

k/all.title: Understanding Health Concepts
k/all.content: demonstrate an awareness of their own health and well-being
demonstrate an understanding of the effects of healthy, active living on the mind and body
investigate the benefits of nutritious foods and explore ways of ensuring healthy eating
practise and discuss appropriate personal hygiene that promotes personal, family, and community health
discuss what action to take when they feel unsafe or uncomfortable, in person or online, and when and how to seek assistance
discuss and demonstrate in play what makes them happy and unhappy, and why

k/all.title: Active Participation
k/all.content: participate actively and regularly in a variety of activities that require the application of movement concepts
participate actively in creative movement and other daily physical activities
demonstrate persistence while engaged in activities that require the use of both large and small muscles
demonstrate strategies for engaging in cooperative play in a variety of games and activities

k/all.title: Movement Skills and Concepts
k/all.content: develop movement skills and concepts as they use their growing bodies to move in a variety of ways and in a variety of contexts
demonstrate spatial awareness in activities that require the use of large muscles
demonstrate control of large muscles with and without equipment
demonstrate balance, whole-body and hand-eye coordination, and flexibility in movement
demonstrate control of small muscles while working in a variety of learning areas and when using a variety of materials or equipment
demonstrate spatial awareness by doing activities that require the use of small muscles

k/all.title: Identity and Self-Image
k/all.content: demonstrate a sense of identity and a positive self-image
recognize personal interests, strengths, and accomplishments
identify and talk about their own interests and preferences
express their thoughts and share experiences

k/all.title: Understanding Perspectives and Canadian Identity
k/all.content: show understanding of the multiple perspectives and diversity among individuals, groups, and communities in Canada, and identify areas of connection
understand that everyone belongs to multiple groups and communities, and that these groups and communities together shape Canadian identity
describe, both verbally and non-verbally, ways in which they contribute to the various groups to which they belong
demonstrate respect for different perspectives and identify areas of connection

k/all.title: Self-Confidence
k/all.content: recognize bias in ideas and develop the self-confidence to stand up for themselves and others against prejudice and discrimination
stand up for themselves, and apply behaviours that enhance their own and others’ well-being
think critically about fair/unfair and biased behaviour towards both themselves and others, and act with compassion and kindness
recognize discriminatory and inequitable practices and behaviours and respond appropriately

k/all.title: People and Communities
k/all.content: demonstrate an awareness of their surroundings
recognize people in their community and talk about what they do
recognize places and buildings within their community, both natural and human-made, and talk about their functions

k/all.title: Respect and Care for Nature
k/all.content: demonstrate an understanding of the natural world and the need to care for and respect the environment
identify similarities and differences between local environments
describe what would happen if something in the local environment changed
describe ways in which they care for and respect the environment

k/all.title: Responding to Art
k/all.content: respond to a variety of forms of dance, drama, music, and visual arts from various cultures and communities, including using their language and mathematics knowledge and skills
express their responses to dance and drama
respond to texts and art forms from various cultures and communities through classroom drama activities and make connections to their own experiences
express their responses to music by moving, by making connections to their own experiences, or by talking about the musical form

k/all.title: Exploring and Creating Art
k/all.content: explore and create a variety of art forms, including dance, drama, music, and visual arts
explore the elements of dance, drama, music, and design
experiment with different materials, techniques, and processes used in a variety of art forms
use problem-solving skills and imagination to create forms of art
communicate ideas through dance, drama, music, and visual arts

4/core-french.title: Listening to Understand
4/core-french.content: determine meaning in a variety of oral French texts, using a range of listening strategies

4/core-french.title: Using Listening Comprehension Strategies
4/core-french.content: identify a range of listening comprehension strategies and use them appropriately before, during, and after listening to understand oral French texts (e.g., identify familiar words and phrases and frequently used expressions; use contextual and/or visual clues in oral texts, including the speaker’s body language and tone of voice, to confirm or clarify meaning; activate prior knowledge and make connections to personal experiences to confirm understanding; ask questions to obtain additional information; visualize, sketch, or draw to record information and ideas)

4/core-french.title: Demonstrating Understanding
4/core-french.content: demonstrate an understanding of the purpose and meaning of oral French texts containing familiar words and expressions about everyday topics and situations, with contextual and visual support (e.g., follow classroom directions; follow a series of Total Physical Response [TPR] commands; sequence a group of pictures or images for a storyboard, based on a description; make drawings to illustrate objects in an oral description; find a specific classroom object by following directions from the teacher and class; identify refrains, rhyme schemes, and other word/sound patterns in songs, poems, read-alouds, chants, and rhymes; listen to a description and identify the object described)

4/core-french.title: Listening to Interact
4/core-french.content: interpret messages accurately while interacting in French for a variety of purposes and with diverse audiences

4/core-french.title: Using Interactive Listening Strategies
4/core-french.content: identify and use interactive listening strategies to suit a variety of situations while participating in social and academic interactions (e.g., demonstrate an understanding of when to listen and when to speak; look at the speaker; listen without interrupting; make connections between personal experiences and what is being said; reconsider their point of view after hearing what others say; repeat a partner’s ideas in their own words as a way of confirming understanding; ask for repetition, confirmation, or clarification of what they hear using phrases such as “Un instant…Je ne comprends pas. Pourriez-vous répéter cela, s’il vous plaît? Qu’est-ce que cela veut dire…?”; use body language such as a nod to indicate understanding and/or agreement)

4/core-french.title: Interacting
4/core-french.content: respond with understanding to what others say while participating in brief, structured interactions about themselves, family, friends, and their immediate environment, with contextual and visual support (e.g., respond appropriately to questions requiring a brief answer in paired and small-group interactions on familiar topics; respond constructively to a partner’s ideas in think-pair-share sessions, using gestures, visual aids, and/or familiar words and phrases; share reactions to a partner’s plans for a celebration or for the weekend)

4/core-french.title: Metacognition
4/core-french.content: (a) describe, in conversation with the teacher and their peers, a few strategies they found helpful before, during, and after listening; (b) identify their areas of greater and lesser strength as listeners, and plan steps they can take to improve their listening skills (e.g., discuss with a partner some strategies and tools that have helped them improve their listening skills; self-monitor listening during a group discussion)

4/core-french.title: Intercultural Understanding
4/core-french.content: demonstrate an understanding of information in oral French texts about aspects of culture in diverse French-speaking communities and other communities around the world, and of French sociolinguistic conventions used in a variety of situations and communities

4/core-french.title: Intercultural Awareness
4/core-french.content: using information from oral French texts, identify French-speaking communities in Ontario, find out about aspects of their cultures, and make connections to personal experiences and their own and other communities (e.g., listen to directions and locate on a map historic Franco-Ontarian or Métis communities such as Sault Ste. Marie or Mattawa; identify examples of the use of French in their immediate environment – such as the bilingual version of the national anthem sung at sports events; listen to a peer describe a family tradition and make connections to a similar tradition in their own family)

4/core-french.title: Awareness of Sociolinguistic Conventions
4/core-french.content: using information from oral French texts, identify and demonstrate an understanding of sociolinguistic conventions used in a variety of situations in diverse French-speaking communities (e.g., formal and informal expressions of courtesy such as different types of salutations; verbal and non-verbal cues appropriate to different environments, such as social gatherings versus classroom contexts; brief expressions used to introduce themselves and others)

4/core-french.title: Speaking to Communicate
4/core-french.content: communicate information and ideas orally in French, using a variety of speaking strategies and age- and grade-appropriate language suited to the purpose and audience

4/core-french.title: Using Oral Communication Strategies
4/core-french.content: identify a range of speaking strategies and use them appropriately to express themselves clearly and coherently in French for various purposes and to a variety of audiences (e.g., use and reuse familiar language structures and patterns, such as repetition, and incorporate previously learned words and phrases to clarify the meaning of oral messages; use visual, nonverbal cues such as gestures, facial expression, body position, and eye contact – pointing, smiling, nodding, leaning forward – and vocal effects such as changes in pitch, tone, pace, and volume to support and clarify meaning; refer to classroom visuals such as anchor charts to help them clarify a message)

4/core-french.title: Producing Oral Communications
4/core-french.content: using familiar words and expressions, produce brief, rehearsed messages in French containing information and ideas about themselves, family, friends, and their immediate environment, with contextual, auditory, and visual support (e.g., describe classroom routines; prepare and deliver a presentation introducing themselves, family members, and/or pets; recount a sequence of events from a fictional or news story; deliver brief, rehearsed oral presentations; give concise directions to a classmate describing how to perform an action or find an object)

4/core-french.title: Speaking with Fluency
4/core-french.content: speak with a smooth pace, appropriate intonation, and accurate pronunciation in brief, rehearsed communications about personal and familiar topics (e.g., use accepted pronunciation for high-frequency words, regularly used phrases, and words with personal significance in brief oral exchanges, dialogues, and presentations; accurately pronounce familiar vocabulary when introducing themselves or their friends and family; speak at a comfortable pace in short, rehearsed question-and-answer routines about familiar topics; pronounce words smoothly and accurately as modelled by the teacher when reciting tongue twisters, chants, rhymes, and newly acquired vocabulary and when participating in choral speaking and/or shared reading activities; use intonation as modelled by the teacher to ask questions; deliver a rehearsed oral presentation at a smooth pace with appropriate phrasing and emphasis)

4/core-french.title: Speaking to Interact
4/core-french.content: participate in spoken interactions in French for a variety of purposes and with diverse audiences

4/core-french.title: Using Speaking Interaction Strategies
4/core-french.content: demonstrate an understanding of appropriate speaking behaviour in a variety of situations (e.g., restate the contributions of other group members to confirm understanding and share preferences; use facial expressions, tone of voice, and gestures that are appropriate to the context and audience; ask questions to clarify the context and purpose for exchanging information)

4/core-french.title: Interacting
4/core-french.content: engage in brief, structured spoken interactions, using familiar words and expressions, with teacher modelling and support (e.g., contribute brief oral instructions and responses in interactive games and role plays; ask and answer questions in surveys and interviews; participate in simulated telephone conversations; answer the teacher’s or their classmates’ questions about their oral presentations)

4/core-french.title: Metacognition
4/core-french.content: (a) describe, in conversation with the teacher and their peers, a few strategies they found helpful before, during, and after speaking to communicate effectively; (b) identify their areas of greater and lesser strength as speakers, and plan steps they can take to improve their speaking skills (e.g., determine the elements of effective presentations; provide feedback on a peer’s oral presentation and listen to peers’ comments about their own presentations; evaluate their use of French in daily interactions with peers and the teacher)

4/core-french.title: Intercultural Understanding
4/core-french.content: in their spoken communications, demonstrate an awareness of aspects of culture in diverse French-speaking communities and other communities around the world, and of the appropriate use of French sociolinguistic conventions in a variety of situations

4/core-french.title: Intercultural Awareness
4/core-french.content: communicate information orally about French-speaking communities in Ontario, including aspects of their cultures and their contributions to la francophonie and the world, and make connections to personal experiences and their own and other communities (e.g., share ideas about the importance of French as demonstrated by its status as an official language of Canada and a required subject in the Ontario elementary curriculum; repeat phrases from songs by Franco-Ontarian musicians that reveal aspects of French Canadian cultures; give brief oral presentations describing traditions and festivals such as le Bal de Neige in Ottawa; use a T-chart to organize information and guide discussions about aspects of Franco-Ontarian cultures, such as family, school life, traditions, and festivals, and make connections to their own culture)

4/core-french.title: Awareness of Sociolinguistic Conventions
